extracted.intended_audience: journal publishers, editorial managers, production staff, and metadata/standards specialists in scholarly publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Defining and adopting a harmonized taxonomy of peer review models and terms across scholarly publishing to reduce confusion, improve transparency, and enable consistent communication and comparison of peer review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key areas of the taxonomy: how reviewer/author identities are exposed or concealed (i.e., the transparency of identity in the review model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The taxonomy defines models of identity transparency to reduce ambiguous or conflicting jargon. The blog notes a recommended naming convention change—replace references to “blind” forms of peer review with “anonymous”—to improve clarity. Implementers should use precise labels for whether identities are revealed, pseudonymized, anonymous, etc., consistent with the ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who the Reviewer interacts with
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key areas of the taxonomy: specification of which people or roles the Reviewer communicates or interacts with during the review process (e.g., authors, editors, other reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and label interaction pathways clearly so stakeholders know whether reviewers see authors, communicate via editors only, can converse with other reviewers, etc. Standardized terms for these interaction models enable consistent description and comparison across journals and platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information shared about the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key areas of the taxonomy: which information about the review process is disclosed or recorded (e.g., review reports, review history, decision rationale, identity metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what metadata and review materials are shared, published, or retained, and use the standardized terms from the NISO recommended practice so readers and stakeholders understand the level of transparency and the boundaries of disclosure. Harmonized wording supports cross-site assessments and metadata interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key areas of the taxonomy: models and policies for commenting or reviewing after an article is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize terminology and practices around post-publication commenting (who may comment, whether comments are moderated or attributed, how they are displayed) so post-publication interactions are consistently described and comparable across publishers and platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology alignment / naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of standardized peer review terminology across systems and platforms so that nomenclature is harmonized, reducing confusion and improving transparency industry-wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog highlights practical mappings and implementation examples (Aries replaced references to “blind” forms of peer review with “anonymous,” and replaced “blind” Editor submission access restrictions with “blocked”) as guidance for publishers and vendors. Publishers, editorial systems, and stakeholders are encouraged to implement ANSI/NISO Z39.106-2023 naming conventions to enable consistent communication, metadata interoperability, and easier comparison of review practices.
